Final explicit review revision of this unexecuted proposal, preserving accepted requirements, all six existing external operation IDs/contracts and business order, all runtime limits and the no-consent rule. Do not change unrelated work. The automatic patches were invalid data bindings, not executable corrections. A read-only compiler replay confirmed that swapping the two lookup operands fixes all four current compiler diagnostics without changing any contract. Correct them with REAL typed TaskValue bindings, not kind:json serialization of binding descriptions.

The exact existing binding shape is:
{"kind":"lookup","port":"reference","items":[{"kind":"output","source":"home_records_value","port":"records"},{"kind":"field","port":"selectedSearchInputIds","items":[{"kind":"output","source":"interpret_home"}]}]}
The product equivalent uses search_records_value.records FIRST and interpret_search_selection.selectedProductIds SECOND. Do not put the identity field in text; it belongs in port. Do not serialize a TaskValue object into a business JSON string. Preserve the existing array-valued consumer loops.

Resolve these remaining concrete review findings using only existing data-adaptation constructs:
1. Selected IDs must be checked against OFFERED candidates before lookup against original records. Current lookups omit that first check. The compact page views already supply offeredSearchInputIds/offeredProductLinkIds. Use existing pure foreach projections to turn those offered scalar IDs into typed records {reference: item}, collect and flatten exactly one level at a time. Validate selected IDs through lookup(offered records, selected IDs) before the existing lookup(original records, selected IDs). Preserve repeated selections, order, all original data and producer action checks. The validated offered lookup must actually be consumed or required before actions; do not emit unused validation. Additional pure projection/validation tasks and their explicit exports are authorized for this correction only. Do not expand extraction to raw snapshots or feed long action URLs into interpretation.
2. Enforce actual blocking at product-page processing too. Current extract_product_row instruction would turn CAPTCHA/access denial/unavailable pages into nullable rows and then allow a successful workbook, contradicting the accepted stop-on-obstacle requirement. Keep explicit business obstacle assessment over compact product facts, followed by a boolean runtime requires before row production/continued work. A missing product field remains an allowed null; a page preventing the requested extraction is a failure, not an invented row. Keep normal Browser cleanup. Do not classify mere cookie information or a nonblocking banner as failure and never interact with consent controls.
3. Ensure original complete-snapshot guards test actual non-null snapshot and both captureTruncated=false and manifestTruncated=false with supported boolean predicates. Do not use objects, arrays or strings as requires. No unconditional blocked-only value task on the successful path.

Keep the already corrected consumer-specific extract.each page views, typed row copying, first-ten ordering without sponsored filtering/deduplication, non-null row objects with nullable fields, real per-product navigation, bounded TSV formatting, actual XLSX writing and writer-derived public file path. Keep requirements byte-for-byte. Every control/action argument must still resolve from original observations. No new operator, executor, inference phase, public interface, architecture or automatic repair authority. Return the complete corrected TaskPlan for validation and separate artifact approval; nothing is approved for execution.
